question: Will any UK cabinet ministers resign in Q1, Q2, Q3, or Q4 of 2026?

content.text: Options resolve Yes if any UK cabinet minister resigns in the corresponding timeframe.
Multiple options can resolve Yes if ministers resign in more than one timeframe. Any option covers the (plausible) event that none resign in 2026.
If government dissolves this will be treated as a resignation.
Full list of cabinet ministers available here:
https://www.gov.uk/government/ministers

question: Burnham recieves a cabinet minister resignation in 2026

content.text: Resolution criteria
This market resolves to
YES
if, between July 23, 2026, and December 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM UTC, any member of the UK Cabinet under Prime Minister Andy Burnham formally resigns from their Cabinet post.
Cabinet Minister Definition:
Any individual officially listed as a member of the Cabinet of the United Kingdom on
GOV.UK
or widely reported by major media outlets (e.g., BBC, The Guardian, Financial Times) as holding a full Cabinet-level role in the Burnham administration.
Resignation Definition:

The minister must voluntarily step down from their Cabinet post (including resignations in protest, for personal reasons, or when requested/pressured to do so by the Prime Minister, provided a formal resignation is submitted and accepted).
Exclusions:
Being sacked, dismissed, or removed directly by the Prime Minister without resigning first.
Being reassigned to a different Cabinet role during a reshuffle.
Temporary leaves of absence (e.g., medical or parental leave) where the minister remains in office.
Leaving office due to death or permanent medical incapacitation.
If no eligible Cabinet minister resigns by the end of December 31, 2026, this market resolves to
NO
Background

Following the resignation of Keir Starmer in June 2026, Andy Burnham (the former Mayor of Greater Manchester) returned to Westminster as the MP for Makerfield, won the Labour leadership unopposed, and was appointed Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on July 20, 2026. Burnham quickly formed his new Cabinet, appointing veteran MP John Healey as Chancellor of the Exchequer, Louise Haigh as First Secretary of State, and shuffling various portfolios to construct his initial team.

Given the swift transition of power and the ongoing factional shifts within the Labour Party following the Starmer-to-Burnham transition, this market tracks the stability of the Burnham Cabinet through the remainder of 2026.
